title: Inner/outer balance
opening: When you hit a tennis ball, you can see where it goes and remember what you felt or noticed in your body during the swing. Compare those details before deciding what to work on; if one does not matter, leave it out.

sides.label: Within
sides.description: What did you feel or think as you played, or what did you notice in your body?

sides.label: Around you
sides.description: What happened around you at the same time? You can name the ball's path, a player's movement or a court condition.

ownPursuit.prompt: Choose a recent situation in your own pursuit. Write what you noticed in yourself and what was happening around you. Which part changes what you do next?
ownPursuit.prediction: What did you feel or think then, or what did you notice in your body?
ownPursuit.observation: What was happening around you in that same moment?
ownPursuit.revision: Do those details change what you think happened or what you would do next? If one part doesn't matter here, leave it out.

accessibility.side: Shift attention between what you notice in yourself and what happens around you
accessibility.ownPursuit: Write and save a reflection about what you noticed in yourself and what was happening around you in a recent situation in your pursuit
accessibility.figure: Illustrative tennis point with two players, a court and a ball path.
